rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī reads the concession sarcastically: even if idols were living and rational, they would be fellow servants, so humans have no basis for making them gods; the next verse refutes even this concession.
rows.anchor: فإن ثبت ذلك فهم عباد أمثالكم ولا فضل لهم عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols means asking them to bring benefits or remove harms; the imperative lām in “let them respond” is a challenge showing their incapacity and unsuitability for worship.
rows.anchor: ومعنى هذا الدعاء طلب المنافع وكشف المضار من جهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition challenges the idolaters to prove their claim that the idols are gods deserving worship.
rows.anchor: أي في ادعاء أنها آلهة ومستحقة للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī compares the argument with Abraham’s rebuke to his father for worshipping what cannot hear, see, or benefit him.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قول إبراهيم عليه السلام لأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since three conclusive proofs show idols are unfit for worship, a rational person should turn only to the God who is powerful, knowing, living, wise, and able to harm and benefit.
rows.anchor: ولما ثبت بهذه الدلائل الثلاثة اليقينية أنها لا تصلح للمعبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four organs matter insofar as they possess the powers of motion and perception: humans exceed lifeless idols, so it is unfitting for the superior to worship an inferior that can neither benefit nor protect.
rows.anchor: فكيف يليق بالأفضل الأكمل الأشرف أن يشتغل بعبادة الأخس الأدون الذي لا يحس منه فائدة البتة

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: Some crude anthropomorphists argue that because lacking bodily organs proves idols are not divine, God must possess those organs or likewise lack divinity.
rows.anchor: تعلق بعض أغمار المشبهة وجها لهم بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects that inference: the verse compares the functional human body with the inert idol to establish human superiority; that comparison is its purpose, not an affirmation of organs for God.
rows.anchor: فهذا هو المقصود من ذكر هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reinforces the preceding proof that idols cannot help their worshippers or themselves: lacking moving limbs and perceiving senses, they cannot benefit or harm, unlike God, who transcends bodily organs yet has perfect power, hearing, and sight.
rows.anchor: الحجة التي ذكرها قبل هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the idolaters used to threaten the Messenger with their gods; the challenge invites them to summon and plot with the idols so their inability to harm him becomes clear.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : إنهم كانوا يخوفون الرسول عليه السلام

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retain the yāʾ in kīdūnī, while the other readers omit it.
rows.anchor: وأثبت نافع وأبو عمرو الياء في

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains the omitted yāʾ by saying verse endings resemble rhymes and Arabic poetry also drops such yāʾs at line ends, citing a verse as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي ، والقول فيه أن الفواصل تشبه القوافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who retain the yāʾ follow the original form.
rows.anchor: والذين أثبتوها فلأن الأصل هو الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not give me respite” means do not delay; the idolaters and their partners are told to hurry their plot.
rows.anchor: أي لا تمهلوني واعجلوا في كيدي أنتم وشركائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal remembrance first leaves an effect in the imagination, then brings increasing illumination to the spirit; those illuminations return through tongue, imagination, and intellect, each stage reinforcing the others, so the knowers’ journey has no end.
rows.anchor: ثم يصعد من ذلك الأثر الخيالي مزيد أنوار وجلايا إلى جوهر الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the address to remember God inwardly appears directed to the Prophet, it applies to every accountable person, each according to the station suited to the capacity of the rational soul.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه عام في حق كل المكلفين ولكل أحد درجة مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging the Messenger to remember God, the verse points to the angels’ constant worship: despite their honor, purity, and freedom from passions, they persist in obedience, so embodied humans have even greater reason to do so.
rows.anchor: لما رغب الله رسوله في الذكر وفي المواظبة عليه ذكر عقيبه ما يقوي دواعيه في ذلك

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists take “those who are with your Lord” to imply that God occupies a place and direction; Rāzī rejects this as impossible on the rational and transmitted proofs given under 7:54 and 10:3.
rows.anchor: المشبهة تمسكوا بقوله : { إن الذين عند ربك } وقالوا لفظ { عند } مشعر بالمكان والجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean divine favor and mercy rather than location, as in the divine report that God is with hearts broken for His sake; this “withness” is not spatial.
rows.anchor: هذه المعية بالفضل والرحمة لا بالجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With your Lord” may mean nearness in honor: a minister is closer in rank to a ruler than a doorkeeper, even when the doorkeeper is physically nearer.
rows.anchor: إن المراد القرب بالشرف . يقال : للوزير قربة عظيمة من الأمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording also honors the angels by associating them with the honored abode where God placed them, the realm of lights, spirits, obedience, and blessings.
rows.anchor: هذا تشريف للملائكة بإضافتهم إلى الله من حيث إنه أسكنهم في المكان الذي كرمه وشرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further sense is that the angels are God’s messengers to creation, like a caliph’s army said to be “with” him although its members are spread across the land.
rows.anchor: لأنهم رسل الله إلى الخلق كما يقال : إن عند الخليفة جيشا عظيما

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm uses the verse to argue that angels are superior to human beings: the Messenger is urged to worship by reference to the angels’ worship, which he says works only if they are superior.
rows.anchor: تمسك أبو بكر الأصم رحمه الله بهذه الآية في إثبات أن الملائكة أفضل من البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order puts glorification first because it is the heart’s knowledge and purification of God, then prostration as bodily action; this shows bodily worship branches from the heart’s acts.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترتيب يدل على أن الأصل في الطاعة والعبودية أعمال القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase restricts the angels’ prostration to God, raising an apparent conflict with their prostration to Adam; Rāzī cites al-Ghazālī’s view that only earthly angels prostrated, not the great heavenly angels.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الغزالي : الذين سجدوا لآدم ملائكة الأرض . فأما عظماء ملائكة السموات فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reconciliation is that the verse’s statement is general while the command to prostrate to Adam is particular, and the particular takes precedence over the general.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا : إن قوله : { وله يسجدون } يفيدون أنهم ما سجدوا لغير الله ، فهذا يفيد العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī links the verse to other descriptions of angels continually standing in worship and surrounding the Throne while praising God.
rows.anchor: وإنا لنحن الصافون * وإنا لنحن المسبحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Anfāl is Medinan except verses 30–36, which are Meccan.
rows.anchor: مدنية إلا من آية : 30 إلى غاية 36 فمكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Anfāl has 75 verses and was revealed after al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وآياتها 75 نزلت بعد البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second interpretation takes the evil as an unbeliever’s spending to oppose Muḥammad and the good as believers’ spending in jihad, such as Abū Bakr’s and ʿUthmān’s support; God gathers the evil wealth and punishes them with it.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : المراد بالخبيث نفقة الكافر على عداوة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, the purpose clause “so God distinguishes” attaches to “they will be gathered”: they are gathered so God can separate the evil party from the good.
rows.anchor: على القول الأول متعلق بقوله : { يحشرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second interpretation, the purpose clause attaches to “then it will be a regret for them,” rather than to “they will be gathered.”
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الثاني متعلق بقوله : { ثم تكون عليهم حسرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those are the losers” refers to the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { أولائك هم الخاسرون } وهو إشارة إلى الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf explains “say to those who disbelieve” as “say on their behalf this statement”; if it meant addressing them directly, the wording would be “if you desist.”
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { قل للذين كفروا } أي قل لأجلهم هذا القول

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is cited for the direct-address wording “if you desist,” supporting the alternative parsing.
rows.anchor: يغفر وقال ابن مسعود هكذا

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If unbelievers abandon disbelief and hostility to the Messenger, enter Islam, and accept its law, God forgives their past disbelief and hostility.
rows.anchor: الكفر وعداوة الرسول ، ودخلوا الإسلام والتزموا شرائعه

words: وَإِن يَعُودُوا۟ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to disbelief and persist, the precedents of earlier peoples apply to them.
rows.anchor: وإن عادوا إليه وإصروا عليه فقد مضت سنة الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the precedent refers to the earlier unbelievers whose plot recoiled upon them at Badr.
rows.anchor: المراد فقد مضت سنة الأولين منهم الذين حاق بهم مكرهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation refers to past nations that united against their prophets; the present unbelievers should expect the same fate if they do not desist.
rows.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الأولين الذين تحزبوا على أنبيائهم من الأمم الذين قد مروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation identifies the precedent with God’s promises that His messengers will prevail and the righteous will inherit the earth.
rows.anchor: وهي قوله : { كتب الله لاغلبن أنا ورسلى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī holds that repentance by a zindīq is accepted; the verse’s promise of forgiveness to those who desist from disbelief covers every kind of unbelief.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها مقبولة لوجوه : الأول : هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one may not know inwardly whether a zindīq has abandoned the heresy, legal judgments rest on appearances; once the person returns, the profession of repentance is accepted.
rows.anchor: أحكام الشرع مبنية على الظواهر ، كما قال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is obligated to repent and has no route to repentance except this act; refusing to accept it would impose an impossible duty.
rows.anchor: لا شك أنه مكلف بالرجوع ولا طريق له إليه إلا بهذه التوبة فلو لم تقبل لزم تكليف ما لا يطاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī also supports acceptance of repentance with the verse stating that God accepts repentance from His servants and pardons sins.
rows.anchor: وهو الذى يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفوا عن السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument assumes reports show three people in the two groups, so one of the groups must consist of a single person.
rows.anchor: ثبت بالروايات أن الطائفتين كانوا ثلاثة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says ṭāʾifa originally means a group, a number able to surround something, but it can also name one person.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : والطائفة في اللغة أصلها الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic expression “a group of believers” in 24:2 shows that a ṭāʾifa may be as small as one person.
rows.anchor: وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s view that ṭāʾifa means one person or more.
rows.anchor: روى الفراء بإسناده عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rationale for calling a person a ṭāʾifa is that someone defending a doctrine continually circles around and protects it, as if with the heart.
rows.anchor: من اختار مذهبا ونصره فإنه لا يزال يكون ذابا عنه ناصرا له

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says Arabic sometimes uses a plural expression for one person, as in saying someone traveled to Mecca on camels.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : العرب توقع لفظ الجمع على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “those to whom the people said” uses the plural “people” for the single Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى يقول : { الذين قال لهم الناس } ( آل عمران : 173 ) يعني نعيم بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation derives the form from ṭāʾif, then adds the feminine ending for emphasis, allowing it to designate one person.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن تكون الطائفة إذا أريد بها الواحد يكون أصلها طائفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī objects that both groups shared unbelief and guilt, so a general cause should not explain punishment assigned to only one; also, past guilt appears not to explain a present punishment.
rows.anchor: والتعذيب يختص بإحدى الطائفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that the second group’s offense was more serious and remained ongoing, which explains its distinct punishment.
rows.anchor: هذا تنبيه على أن جرم الطائفة الثانية كان أغلظ وأقوى من جرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female hypocrites share the same qualities of hypocrisy; “some are of some” means their way is one, with no real distinction between them.
rows.anchor: أنت مني وأنا منك ، أي أمرنا واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar includes every ugly deed, especially denying the Messenger; maʿrūf includes every good deed, especially belief in the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ولفظ المنكر يدخل فيه كل قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take “they clench their hands” as withholding every good; Rāzī prefers withholding obligatory charity, including zakat and spending in God’s path, since only abandoning an obligation is censured.
rows.anchor: وقيل عن كل خير واجب من زكاة وصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image comes from a giver extending an open hand, so a miser who refuses to give is described as closing the hand.
rows.anchor: المعطي يمد يده ويبسطها بالعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording cannot mean literal forgetfulness: human forgetfulness is involuntary and does not merit blame, while forgetfulness is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن إجراؤه على ظاهره لأنا لو حملناه على النسيان على الحقيقة لما استحقوا عليه ذما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that they abandoned God’s command until it was like something forgotten, so He left them as forgotten with respect to reward and mercy; the wording parallels the “evil recompense” in 42:40.
rows.anchor: تركوا أمره حتى صار بمنزلة المنسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes forgetting the opposite of remembering: they left worship and praise of God, so He left remembering them with mercy and kindness; “forgetting” names the consequence of not remembering.
rows.anchor: فلما تركوا ذكر الله بالعبادة والثناء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the hypocrites fāsiqūn means they are complete or extreme in their impiety.
rows.anchor: أي هم الكاملون في الفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing hypocrites’ corrupt deeds and threatening them, the passage presents believers’ good qualities in opposition and then promises them lasting reward.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بالغ في وصف المنافقين بالأعمال الفاسدة والأفعال الخبيثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites are “some from others” because followers’ hypocrisy grows from ancestral models, imitation, appetite, and habit; believers are “allies” because their bond comes through shared reasoning, divine guidance, and enabling grace.
rows.anchor: بل بسبب المشاركة في الاستدلال والتوفيق والهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wilāya is the opposite of enmity and its root sense is nearness; enmity is named from crossing beyond or away.
rows.anchor: الأصل في لفظ الولاية القرب

words: يَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five marks distinguishing believers from hypocrites are commanding right, forbidding wrong, prayer, zakat, and obedience: unlike hypocrites, believers do not command evil, pray lazily, withhold obligatory wealth, or shirk and discourage jihad.
rows.anchor: فذكر هذه الأمور الخمسة التي بها يتميز المؤمن من المنافق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle sīn in “God will have mercy on them” emphasizes certainty and force, like a promise of eventual revenge; Rāzī compares other future promises.
rows.anchor: وذكر حرف السين في قوله

rows.speaker: أصحاب هذا القول
rows.claim: One view says a vow includes both a promise spoken aloud and an intention formed silently; its proponents read the passage’s mention of secrets and private counsel as evidence.
rows.anchor: أصحاب هذا القول إن قوله : { ومنهم من عاهد الله } كان شيئا نووه في أنفسهم

rows.speaker: المعتمر بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān recounts that during a violent sea wind he silently intended a vow, then asked his father about it after reaching Basra; his father told him to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: يروى عن المعتمر بن سليمان

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The jurists whom Rāzī calls the investigators hold that a vow is binding only when spoken aloud, citing the Prophetic statement that inner thoughts are pardoned unless uttered.
rows.anchor: وقال المحققون : هذه المعاهدة مقيدة بما إذا حصل التلفظ بها باللسان

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: They also argue that “if God gives us of His bounty, we will give charity” reports a spoken commitment, as its wording indicates an utterance.
rows.anchor: وظاهره مشعر بالقول باللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī distinguishes voluntary charity, obligations imposed directly by religious law, and obligations a person incurs by making a vow, and asks which kinds the promise to give charity covers.
rows.anchor: والواجب قسمان : قسم وجب بإلزام الشرع ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voluntary charity is excluded: the verse calls their refusal miserliness, which in legal usage means withholding an obligation, and a person is not blameworthy for leaving a recommended gift.
rows.anchor: والبخل في عرف الشرع عبارة عن منع الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse certainly includes duties imposed by religious law, such as zakat, wealth needed for pilgrimage or fighting, and required maintenance.
rows.anchor: فالذي يجب بإلزام الشرع داخل تحت الآية لا محالة
